idiom_name: AndroidX NavHost/NavController destinations + ViewModel with StateFlow for syncing
implementation_notes: On Android the framework owns the views: FragmentManager holds the fragments attached to an activity (add/replace/hide transactions, addToBackStack for the back stack, findFragmentByTag as the lookup) and the Navigation component generalises it to destinations that a NavController switches inside a NavHost, with the back stack as the registry order. State is synced with ViewModel + StateFlow - the screen collects the flow and re-renders - so the handler decides which view exists, not what it displays. Declarative Compose replaces fragments with composables and a NavHost, where the current destination and its arguments are ordinary state. In both forms the retained view is framework-owned, so keep hand-written bookkeeping to the minimum the framework does not provide, and treat the ViewModel as the home of per-screen state.
pitfalls: replace() in a fragment transaction destroys the previous fragment's view and its state, so per-screen state belongs in the ViewModel (or in the back stack's saved state), never in fragment fields.
commit() is asynchronous and throws IllegalStateException after onSaveInstanceState; commit state changes with commitNow() or the extensions' commit { } before the lifecycle has saved state.
A ViewModel must never hold Activity, View or fragment references - including a registry of views - or the whole activity leaks across configuration changes.
Collecting a StateFlow without repeatOnLifecycle keeps updating a stopped UI and can crash; tie the collector to the view lifecycle instead.
